specs.title: AC-41: The form renders first name, last name, email, confirm email, phone number and a terms checkbox
AC-42: First name and last name are required and must be at least 2 characters
AC-43: Email is required and must be a valid address; confirm email must match it
AC-44: Phone number is optional; when filled it must be exactly 9 digits
AC-45: The terms checkbox is required

AC-46: The pay button is enabled whenever no payment request is in flight; clicking it on an invalid form marks all fields as touched, shows the messages and shows the toast The form contains errors, without navigating

AC-47: The pay button on a valid form sends POST /reservations, is disabled while the request is in flight, navigates to /confirmation on success, and on failure stays on the form and shows the toast Payment failed. Please try again.
AC-61: The checkout shows the title Your details
AC-62: The pay button reads Pay <total> PLN, the total of the booking
AC-63: Back on the checkout returns to the summary with the booking intact
AC-64: The checkout values survive going back to the summary and forward again, and a page reload; a new booking starts with an empty form
AC-65: The labels of the five required fields end with *; the phone label does not
AC-68: Every checkout identifier in section 9.4 is present with the exact names and values given there

AC-48: /confirmation shows Payment successful and Your tickets will be sent shortly to <email>; Continue navigates to / and clears the booking; the booking survives a reload via sessionStorage; entering the summary, checkout or confirmation without a matching booking redirects to /
AC-69: Every confirmation identifier in section 9.5 is present with the exact names and values given there
AC-01: Without a chosen date, / shows today's screenings: one movie card per movie with a screening today
AC-02: Each card shows title, genre, runtime in minutes and format (PL dubbing / PL subtitles)
AC-03: Each card renders one button per screening of that movie on the selected day, labelled with the screening time (HH:mm), ordered by time
AC-04: Clicking a screening button navigates to /screenings/:id/seats for that screening id
AC-49: While the movie request is in flight, / shows a loading indicator and no movie cards
AC-50: When the movie request fails, / shows Failed to load movies and a Retry button that re-issues the request
AC-51: Every movie-list identifier in section 9.1 is present with the exact names and values given there
AC-52: Above the movie list, the day picker shows Today and the next four days by English weekday name, followed by a datepicker; Today is selected by default
AC-53: Choosing another day shows only the movies with a screening on that day, each with only that day's screenings
AC-54: A day without screenings shows No screenings on this day and no movie cards
AC-55: The selected day is kept in the URL as ?date=YYYY-MM-DD; opening such a URL selects that day, and a missing, invalid or past date selects today
AC-66: Every seat-selection identifier in section 9.2, and the toast identifier in section 9.6, is present with the exact names and values given there
AC-05: The seat map has 15 rows, numbered 1 to 15, row 1 rendered directly under the screen
AC-06: Rows 11 to 15 contain 24 columns; rows 1 to 10 contain columns 5 to 24 only
AC-07: A two-seat-wide gap is rendered between columns 4 and 5 and between columns 20 and 21 in every row; gaps carry no seat and no number
AC-08: Column numbering is global 1–24 and identical across rows; in rows 1–10, numbering starts at 5
AC-09: The row number is rendered on both the left and the right edge of every row
AC-10: Every seat renders its column number
AC-11: A SCREEN indicator is rendered above row 1
AC-12: Row 1, columns 10 to 15 are accessible seats — 6 of them
AC-13: Row 15 renders 12 couches, each spanning two adjacent columns: 1–2, 3–4, … 23–24
AC-14: A couch is rendered as one wide element, visually distinct from a single seat
AC-15: The total number of selectable elements in the auditorium is 308 (200 seats in rows 1–10, 96 in rows 11–14, 12 couches in row 15)
AC-56: The seat selection shows the title Choose your seats and the subtitle Show Date: <Weekday> <D> <Mon> <HH:mm> of the screening
AC-57: Above the seat map, horizontally centred over it, the text You can reserve up to 10 seats per reservation is shown
AC-16: Seats listed in occupiedSeats for the screening are rendered unavailable and cannot be selected
AC-17: A couch is unavailable when either of its two seat identifiers is in occupiedSeats
AC-18: Clicking an available seat selects it; clicking it again deselects it
AC-19: Clicking a couch selects both of its seats as one unit; it cannot be half-selected
AC-20: Selection is capped at 10 seats; a couch counts as 2
AC-21: A click that would exceed 10 seats is ignored and shows the toast Maximum 10 seats per booking
AC-22: At the cap, already selected seats and couches can still be deselected
AC-58: Between the seat map and the Cancel / Continue buttons, the selected-seats panel shows Selected seats: <n> and one Row <r>: <seats> line per row, updated on every selection change
AC-23: The legend lists exactly Available, Selected, Unavailable, Accessible
AC-24: Available seats use #2E7D32
AC-25: Selected seats use #F9A825
AC-26: Unavailable seats use #C62828
AC-27: Accessible seats use #1565C0
AC-33: Cancel navigates to / and clears the selection
AC-34: Continue navigates to /screenings/:id/summary
AC-35: Continue does nothing when no seat is selected
AC-36: Each selected item is listed with movie title, screening date, time, row number, seat description and price
